newsitem.title: UK: Oil loadings in North Sea blocked by fishermen.
newsitem.headline: Oil loadings in North Sea blocked by fishermen.

text.p: The Shetland Island oil port of Sullom Voe has been blockaded by a small group of fishing vessels which has halted tanker traffic to and from the port, a port official said on Monday.
"It started at 0700 a.m. (0600 GMT) this morning and no movements are planned for the moment or the rest of the day," the official said.
The official said that the blockade was formed by 11 small shell fishing boats. He said he had been given no indication of how long the blockade would last.
"They are refusing to respond (on the radio)," he said.
The port of Sullom Voe is the export terminal for world benchmark North Sea Brent blend crude.
The port exports an average of about 480,000 barrels per day of crude.
"One (crude tanker) vessel is scheduled to sail tomorrow morning. And possibly one vessel to berth tomorrow night," the port official said.

The crews of the fishing boats are protesting against a lack of full compensation from the International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund (IOCF) following the Braer tanker disaster four years ago, said the official.
